data.narrative:
Cortical Labs is a Series A–stage AI & Software company that has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis triangulates across a universe of five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers, supplemented by one public comparable (Palantir, PLTR) and eight private peers including Scale AI, Reflection AI, Waymo, Figure AI, and others.

Two methods were applied. Stage-progression methodology, using total raised as a proxy base and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yields $22M. Peer-median analysis across the five-company comp set—comprising Scale AI ($29.0B, Series B), Reflection AI ($25.0B, Series A), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B, Series B), Black Forest Labs ($3.2B, Series B), and Field AI ($2.0B, Series B)—produces a median valuation of $5.6B, with a range spanning $2.0B to $29.0B.

The wide variance between methods reflects fundamental uncertainty in early-stage AI valuations. Stage-progression anchors to capital efficiency ($22M), while peer-median is dominated by outlier valuations in the frontier-AI subsector. A triangulated range of $19M to $6.4B, with a median of $2.8B, reflects this tension. The appropriate valuation likely falls materially below the peer median given Cortical Labs' earlier stage relative to most comparables; however, without revenue, profitability, or product-market traction data, precision is limited. Key uncertainties include the company's actual progress on core technology, customer validation, and burn rate relative to raised capital.
